brief.outcome: Launch a podcast for engineers moving into management within eight weeks, and reach at least 4 discovery calls booked a month from it within six months, within the budget.

ambition.goal_beyond: The podcast keeps bringing the right engineers to your calls and turning into coaching clients, not only listeners.
rungs: Launch the podcast on time with good-sounding episodes on the main listening apps.
Build the show around the call goal and trace every booked call to where it came from, so you know which episodes and channels bring calls and can cut what does not.
Keep it working: a monthly check of calls by source and a simple routine that repurposes each episode, so the flow of calls does not depend on one lucky episode.
ambition.judge: Calendly's own meeting records, exported with the source of each booking (tagged links and a how-did-you-hear question), counted per month.

brief.deliverable: A launched podcast: show plan, first episodes edited and published to the main listening apps, a call-to-action page with a Calendly link that records where each booking came from, promotion posts and emails, and a monthly readout of booked calls against the target of 4.
done: Format (interview or solo), cadence and launch date chosen by you from ranked options
Booking path tested: a test booking shows its source in the Calendly export
Show brief, episode plan and call-to-action page ready and approved by you
First episodes recorded by you and edited to a stated quality bar
Feed validated, submitted and published only with your yes for each step
Spend tracked against $1,500 setup and $200 a month
Monthly readout of calls booked by source against 4 a month

metric.name: Discovery calls booked per month that come from the podcast

The weekly time needed fits what the owner can give (set at the decision)

answers.question: What is the business and audience?
answers.answer: Career coach for engineers moving into management. 4,000 LinkedIn followers and an email list of 1,200.

answers.question: What should the podcast do, and by when?
answers.answer: Bring at least 4 discovery calls a month within six months. Launch within eight weeks.

answers.question: Budget and skills?
answers.answer: $1,500 for setup and $200 a month after. A decent microphone but no editing skills.

answers.question: Tools, data home and who decides?
answers.answer: Calendly for calls. Keep files in this project. I decide.

answers.question: My guess for what should happen after this (ambition)
answers.answer: Accepted as the working guess: you want the podcast to keep bringing the right engineers to calls, so we trace every call to its source and keep what works.

research.approach: Practitioners treat a business podcast as a content channel with a booking path, and fix the path first: one clear call to action, a tagged scheduling link per channel and a how-did-you-hear question, so booked calls are counted rather than guessed from downloads. They define one listener and one promise, choose a format they can sustain every week, and launch with at least three episodes so new listeners have something to binge, with a few more recorded ahead. They submit the feed early, check it plays in listening apps and on each platform, then spend the first month promoting to the warm audience in two or three ways they can keep up, asking a small group of target listeners what they expected and where their attention dropped. After the launch they pull clips, a key point and a discussion question from each episode for posts and emails. They read results by what people do next (clicks, bookings), not downloads alone, and decide what to repeat, improve or stop.

sources.title: Podcast requirements (Apple Podcasts for Creators)
sources.note: Page shows no publication date; accessed 2026-11-03. Platform rules for the feed: RSS 2.0, public, UTF-8, at least one episode with a unique enclosure and a never-changing GUID, consistent tag casing, artwork and content guidelines.

sources.title: What to do in the first 30 days after launching a podcast (The Podcast Haven)
sources.note: Practitioner guide: days 1 to 3 confirm distribution on each platform with a second person doing quality control; days 4 to 7 ask target listeners; week 2 pull clips and takeaways and pick two or three promotion methods; measure starts, retention, link clicks.

steps.name: Define one listener, one promise and what the audience already responds to
steps.why: A show for one listener with a clear promise is easier to find and to talk about than a general coaching show.

steps.name: Build and test the booking path with source tracking
steps.why: The goal is booked calls, so every channel needs a tagged link and a how-did-you-hear question that a test booking proves.

steps.name: Choose format, cadence and budget the owner can sustain
steps.why: A show that stops after a few episodes brings no calls; the owner has no editing skills and a fixed budget.

steps.name: Plan the episodes and the edit to a quality bar
steps.why: Launch with at least three episodes and more recorded ahead; clean audio and distinct titles matter for first impressions.

steps.name: Validate the feed and publish to the listening apps
steps.why: A feed that fails Apple's rules or does not play delays the launch.

steps.name: Promote to the warm audience and turn each episode into posts and emails
steps.why: Two or three promotion methods done well beat many done once; clips and takeaways keep the show visible.

steps.name: Read calls by source, ask early listeners, then repeat, improve or stop
steps.why: Downloads alone do not show whether the show brings clients.

pitfalls.text: Counting downloads as success when the goal is booked calls, or losing the source of calls because links are not tagged.
Launching a feed with errors, or with one episode, so it is rejected or looks thin.
Choosing a format the owner cannot keep up weekly, such as interviews with heavy booking and editing.
Spreading promotion across too many channels so none is done well.

stages.name: Confirm the brief
stages.goal: Turn the owner's words into a measured goal, budget and what is unknown. Writes BRIEF.md.

stages.name: Pull what the audience already responds to
stages.goal: Gather past bookings with how clients found the owner, LinkedIn post results by topic and the email list's size and engagement into one working folder.

checks.name: Meeting count in the file matches the Calendly export's row count exactly
Owner-reported figures are labelled as reported
Missing data is named with what it would unlock

stages.name: Test the booking path
stages.goal: Give the owner exact steps to add a how-did-you-hear question and a tagged link in Calendly, then read the export to check a test booking shows its source. The owner makes the Calendly changes and the test booking; we only read the export. Write one tagged link per channel.

outputs.name: Booking path check and tagged links

checks.name: A test booking from a tagged link appears in the export with its source, and is then cancelled
The how-did-you-hear question is live on the discovery event and its answers appear in the export
Ends with CHECKED, LIMITED or UNRELIABLE and what that means for counting calls

stages.name: What show fits this audience and goal?
stages.goal: Test which listener, topics and format fit the data and the budget, and work out what the first audience can supply toward 4 calls a month. State the gap honestly.

checks.name: Every hypothesis is SUPPORTED, REFUTED or UNKNOWN with the figure behind it
Funnel maths shows listeners, clicks and bookings at low, middle and high assumptions beside 4 calls a month, with each rate labelled as an assumption
The main finding names a competing explanation

stages.name: Rank formats, cadence and budget splits
stages.goal: Offer three to five ranked show designs (for example solo weekly, interviews every two weeks, short episodes) each with weekly owner hours, spend in the $1,500 and $200 limits, expected calls, confidence and risk.

checks.name: Every option cites the finding it rests on
Every option lists each cost line and totals within $1,500 setup and $200 a month, or says it does not
Every option states weekly owner hours

stages.name: Owner chooses the show
stages.goal: The owner picks format, cadence, launch date, how editing is handled and the success rule for calls. Ask why when the top option is passed over.

checks.name: Chosen and passed-over options are recorded with reasons
The go, adjust or stop rule for calls has numbers and dates

stages.name: Write the show pack and call-to-action page
stages.goal: Write the show name options, description, artwork brief, first six episode plans with run sheets (and guest outreach and a guest release if interviews), show notes template, the call-to-action page with the tagged Calendly link, and the promotion posts and emails for the first month.

checks.name: Every episode and post makes one ask and links to the tagged booking link for its channel
Episode titles are distinct and say what the episode covers
No client name, story or result appears without written permission on file
No promise of promotion, pay rise or job outcome from coaching

stages.name: Brief the audio edit and set the quality bar
stages.goal: Write the editor brief and quality checklist for the first three or more episodes: cuts, intro and outro, levels, noise, and chapter marks. The owner records; a hired editor or tool does the edit. Then check each edit against the bar.

owner.gap: A podcast audio editor and producer who can edit and mix episode audio

checks.name: Each episode is listened to end to end by someone other than the editor and passes the written checklist before it is published
Editor cost per episode is quoted and fits the monthly limit
Raw recordings are kept in the project until the show has run three months

stages.name: Validate, publish and promote
stages.goal: Register the launch with its rule and baseline, set up the host, validate the feed, submit it, publish at least three episodes, then send the promotion posts and emails, one approved action at a time.

checks.name: The rule and baseline are in experiments.jsonl before the first public post
The feed passes Apple's validator and plays in at least two listening apps with the right title, artwork and links before submission
At least three episodes are live at launch
Each purchase is approved by the owner and logged against $1,500 and $200 a month

stages.name: Read calls by source
stages.goal: Each month export Calendly bookings with their source and set them beside downloads, listens and link clicks per episode, against 4 calls a month and the spend limits.

checks.name: Calls come from the Calendly export with a source; calls with no source are shown separately
Spend to date is shown against both limits
A channel or episode is called better only with at least 3 months of data or 10 bookings; before that INCONCLUSIVE

stages.name: Repeat, improve or stop
stages.goal: Close the experiment, save rules with their scope, and decide what to repeat, improve or stop for the next three months.

checks.name: The experiment is closed in experiments.jsonl with a verdict
Each saved rule says whether it applies to this show or to any show
A repeat, improve or stop decision is written for each channel and format

hypotheses.statement: The 4,000 followers and 1,200 emails alone cannot supply enough first listeners for 4 calls a month.
hypotheses.test: Funnel maths from the audience that is engaged (LinkedIn clicks, email clickers) times assumed listen, click and booking rates, at low, middle and high.
hypotheses.confirm_if: At the middle assumption the first 90 days give fewer than 4 booked calls a month.
hypotheses.refute_if: At the low assumption the warm audience already gives 4 or more booked calls a month.

hypotheses.statement: Today's calls cannot be traced to a source, so the podcast's calls would be invisible.
hypotheses.test: Check the past-bookings export for source or how-heard values; run a test booking from a tagged link.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Fewer than half of past bookings have a source, or the test booking shows no source.
hypotheses.refute_if: Most past bookings have a source and the test booking shows its source.

hypotheses.statement: A few topics on the first-time manager move draw most of the audience's interest, and a general coaching show would dilute them.
hypotheses.test: LinkedIn impressions, comments and clicks by topic, and email clicks by topic, over 12 months.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Three or fewer topics account for at least half of the clicks and comments across 10 or more posts.
hypotheses.refute_if: Engagement is spread evenly across topics with no clear leaders.

hypotheses.statement: Interviews would cost more weekly hours and edit cost than the owner's limits allow.
hypotheses.test: Compare weekly hours and per-episode edit cost for solo versus interview in the options with the owner's hours and the $200 a month limit.
hypotheses.confirm_if: The interview design needs more weekly hours than the owner can give or edit cost above the monthly limit.
hypotheses.refute_if: Both designs fit the hours and the monthly limit.

hypotheses.statement: Listeners hear the call to action but do not click through to book.
hypotheses.test: Link clicks per episode against downloads, and bookings against clicks, after launch.
hypotheses.confirm_if: Clicks are under 1% of listeners of an episode, or clicks happen but fewer than one in ten clickers book.
hypotheses.refute_if: Clicks and bookings follow the funnel rates assumed in the diagnosis.

measurement.window: Monthly for six months from launch; compare calls in months 4 to 6 with the 12-month booking baseline.
measurement.min_volume: At least 10 bookings or 3 months of data before calling a channel or episode type better; before that the verdict is INCONCLUSIVE.
measurement.stop_rule: Review the format if setup spend passes $1,500, monthly spend passes $200, or the owner misses two scheduled episodes in a row; otherwise run the full window.
